Prompt Guide research record, reviewed 2026-10-19. Public practices support explicit outcomes, relevant context, clear tools, and outcome verification. Sources: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompting and https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents . Bloom https://www.anthropic.com/research/bloom documents automated behavioral evaluation, not guaranteed self-certification. Historical context-position and intrinsic self-correction papers establish scoped results, not universal current-model laws. Claims of universal internal Obsidian workflows remain unverified. Full provenance and limitations: research/sources.md and research/claims.md in https://github.com/MananPoojara/Prompt-guide .

Prompt Guide measured results, executed 2026-10-19 with Codex CLI 0.163.0, gpt-6.1-sol, reasoning effort none. Extraction pilot: one attempt per variant, four synthetic notes per attempt; baseline and candidate both matched 4/4 records, a tie. No evidence of candidate superiority, repeated-run reliability, or generalization. Coding demonstration: search normalization changed 3 failures in 5 tests into 5 passes, confirmed independently with unchanged tests. One small demonstration, not a benchmark. Evidence: labs/prompt-contract and labs/search-fix in https://github.com/MananPoojara/Prompt-guide .

Prompt Guide scope correction from the user, 2026-10-19: this is a public resource showing real AI engineering, not a course, homework, or assignment. Lead with original publicly released prompts, named engineers' documented experiments, diagrams, actual inputs/outputs, and the surrounding skills, plugins, MCP, harnesses, loops, and graphs. Keep our authored templates separate. Never claim access to undisclosed private lab prompting styles. This supersedes the earlier lesson-first framing. Current artifacts: originals/manifest.json pins six licensed Anthropic/OpenAI prompt artifacts; cases/ contains provenance and workflow case studies. An X launch draft exists but is not posted.
